headline: Air Liquide completes 'golden weld' connecting its Rotterdam capture plant to the Porthos CO2 pipeline
summary: Air Liquide made the 'golden weld' physically tying its Cryocap cryogenic capture unit at Rozenburg into the shared Porthos CO2 transport-and-storage network in Rotterdam; captured CO2 will flow via the Maasvlakte compressor station to the offshore P18-A depleted gas field. Air Liquide is one of Porthos's four foundation customers (with Shell, Air Products and ExxonMobil); Porthos is targeted to start up in H2 2027 at the earliest.
co2crc_note: An open-access, multi-user offshore CO2 T&S hub reaching construction milestones is a direct reference model for Australian shared-infrastructure CCS hubs such as CarbonNet.
extractor_note: Construction connection milestone within an FID'd project; Porthos not yet operational (H2 2027 target). org_types: 'infrastructure' is not a listed ORG_TYPE — closest is 'other'; Porthos is the T&S JV. See extractor_note.

headline: Climeworks wins ~£0.78m UK government tender to supply direct-air-capture removal credits
summary: Swiss direct-air-capture developer Climeworks won a £783,749 (~US$1.04m) UK government tender to supply carbon-removal credits offsetting construction emissions of a new government building, part of a broader ~£2.5m government carbon-credit procurement.
co2crc_note: Public-sector procurement of durable engineered removals (rather than avoidance offsets) is a demand-side signal Australian CDR and storage developers can point to when building an offtake case.
extractor_note: £783,749 is a government procurement award for removal credits (a supplier contract paid with public money); recorded as government-funding.

headline: Rio Tinto and Shougang commission an industrial-scale blast-furnace CO2-capture trial at Jingtang, China
summary: Rio Tinto and Chinese steelmaker Shougang commissioned an industrial-scale facility capturing CO2 from blast-furnace gas at Shougang's Jingtang base — processing up to 3,000 m3/h of blast-furnace gas and capturing up to 10,000 t/yr of CO2 using waste heat — and are exploring converting captured CO2 into syngas for reuse in steelmaking. Underlying announcement was 28 Sep, one day outside the daily window.
co2crc_note: Industrial-scale steel-sector blast-furnace CO2 capture, with an Australian mining major as partner, is a hard-to-abate capture benchmark relevant to Australia's steel/minerals decarbonisation.
extractor_note: Radar/near-miss: 28 Sep announcement, one day out of the daily window. capacity_mtpa from up-to-10,000 t/yr (0.01 Mtpa). Rio Tinto classed 'OG-major' as the closest listed large-corporate type (it is a mining major, not oil & gas).
